goal: Let nodes fetch and verify a UTXO set snapshot directly over P2P instead of trusting a third-party download for assumeutxo.
Aims to remove the UX and trust barrier that currently limits assumeutxo adoption.
reviewability: Stale: needs rebase and CI is failing, with no author activity for over 100 days.
PR is in draft awaiting rework to match an evolving external BIP, so review now would likely be invalidated.
agreement: Disputed: six contributors gave concept NACKs, arguing this degrades P2P trust-minimization (evoskuil, eynhaender, stickies-v, l0rinc, narula, nkaretnikov).
Concept ACKs from others who found the feature valuable and demoed it working (andrewtoth, svanstaa, danielabrozzoni).
Verified by testing a full download and activation on mainnet (svanstaa).
Unaddressed objection: a malicious peer can trigger large allocations before merkle verification, no fix yet (andrewtoth).
Unresolved design question on RPC height handling, no final decision (danielabrozzoni, stickies-v).

categories.name: kernel
why: P4 because the change is only a metadata field added to chainparams data, not a kernel API change.
Does not affect what libbitcoinkernel exposes or how it can be used as a library.

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it removes third-party trust dependency for assumeutxo, a real usability gain if the concept is accepted.
A reviewer demoed a full working download and snapshot activation end to end on mainnet.
Not P1 because nothing else in the project depends on it, and whether the network should carry this data at all is unresolved.

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because the new RPC is just a thin driver for the underlying P2P feature.
Its value rises and falls with the feature it exposes rather than standing on its own.

categories.name: tools
why: P4 because it is a narrow, single-purpose helper script for computing a merkle root.
No independent user base beyond supporting this one feature.

categories.name: validation
why: P4 because the touch to validation.cpp is a single log line with no logic change.
The chainparams data addition supports P2P verification rather than affecting consensus or chainstate correctness.
